content.title: Meeting your partner's parents
content.scenario: Win over your partner's parents at dinner and dodge the wedding talk.

rounds.situation: You arrive for dinner at your partner's family home. Their parents, Tito Ben and Tita Lorna, open the door.
rounds.tagalog: Magandang gabi po, Tito, Tita. May dala po akong leche flan, sana magustuhan ninyo.
rounds.translation: Good evening, Tito, Tita. I brought some leche flan; I hope you like it.

chunks.note: A partner's parents are usually Tito and Tita, always with po.

chunks.tagalog: May dala po akong leche flan,
chunks.note: Never arrive empty-handed: 'may dala' means you brought something along.
Ninyo is the respectful 'you' here, as the ones doing the liking.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet both parents respectfully and offer the dessert you brought.

rounds.situation: Dinner is served, and Tita Lorna's kare-kare is excellent. She watches you take the first bite.
rounds.tagalog: Ang sarap po ng kare-kare ninyo, Tita! Kayo po ba mismo ang nagluto nito?
rounds.translation: Your kare-kare is so delicious, Tita! Did you cook this yourself?

chunks.tagalog: Ang sarap po ng kare-kare ninyo, Tita!
chunks.english: your kare-kare is so delicious, Tita!
chunks.note: Ang + adjective is an exclamation: 'so tasty!'. Po sits right after the first word.
Mismo means 'yourself, in person'; ba turns it into a question.
Nagluto = cooked (completed action).

rounds.speakingPrompt: Compliment her cooking warmly and ask whether she made it herself.

rounds.situation: Tito Ben puts down his spoon and asks what you do for a living. This is your chance to sound serious.
rounds.tagalog: Nagtatrabaho po ako sa isang BPO sa Makati, at nag-iipon na rin po kami para sa sariling bahay.
rounds.translation: I work at a BPO in Makati, and we're already saving up for a house of our own.

chunks.note: Nagtatrabaho is the ongoing aspect: 'am working'.
BPO (outsourcing, call centres) stays in English, as in any Manila conversation.

chunks.tagalog: at nag-iipon na rin po kami
chunks.english: and we're already saving up too
chunks.note: Kami is 'we' without the listener: you and your partner, not Tito.

chunks.english: for a house of our own
chunks.note: Sarili + -ng = 'own'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell him where you work and that the two of you are saving for a home.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Nagtatrabaho po ako sa isang BPO sa Makati, at nag-iipon na rin po kami para sa sariling bahay.

rounds.situation: Tita Lorna leans in with a big smile and asks when the wedding is. The whole table goes quiet.
rounds.tagalog: Naku, Tita, pinag-uusapan na po namin 'yan. Pero siyempre, gusto muna naming maging handa talaga.
rounds.translation: Oh, Tita, we're already talking about it. But of course, we want to be truly ready first.

chunks.note: Naku buys you a second and keeps the mood light.
Pinag-uusapan = being discussed (ongoing); namin = by us.

chunks.tagalog: gusto muna naming maging handa talaga.
chunks.english: we want to be really ready first
chunks.note: Muna means 'first, for now': the polite way to buy time.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Laugh it off gently: say you're discussing it, but want to be ready first.

rounds.situation: The evening is over. As you leave, you take each parent's hand for the traditional blessing.

rounds.translation: Bless me, Tito, Tita. Thank you for the wonderful dinner; next time I'll do the cooking.

chunks.tagalog: Salamat po sa napakasarap na hapunan.

chunks.note: Napaka- + adjective = 'very, so'.

chunks.tagalog: Next time, ako na po ang magluluto.
chunks.english: next time, I'll be the one cooking
chunks.note: Magluluto is the future aspect; 'ako na' = 'let me take over'.

lessons.summary: Share family gossip with your best friend and swear them to secrecy.

content.title: Chismis with your best friend
content.scenario: Share family gossip with your best friend and swear them to secrecy.

rounds.situation: You're having merienda with your best friend at a cafe. You can't hold the news in any longer.
rounds.tagalog: Bes, may chika ako sa'yo, pero promise, sa ating dalawa lang 'to, ha?
rounds.translation: Bestie, I've got some gossip for you, but promise this stays between the two of us, okay?

chunks.english: bestie, I've got some news for you
chunks.note: Bes (from bestie) works for any close friend; chika = gossip, the latest.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.

chunks.english: this stays between the two of us, okay?
chunks.note: Ha? at the end asks for agreement, like 'okay?'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell your friend you have juicy news, and make them promise to keep it secret.

rounds.situation: Your friend leans in. Spill it: your cousin Mark has secretly proposed to his girlfriend Liza.
rounds.tagalog: 'Yung pinsan kong si Mark, nag-propose na raw kay Liza, pero hindi pa alam ni Tita Baby!
rounds.translation: Apparently my cousin Mark proposed to Liza, but Tita Baby doesn't know yet!

chunks.note: Opening with 'yung + the person sets up the story, very conversational.
Raw (daw after consonants) = 'reportedly': the essential gossip word.

chunks.tagalog: pero hindi pa alam ni Tita Baby!
chunks.english: but Tita Baby doesn't know yet!
chunks.note: Hindi pa = not yet.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Share the news you heard about your cousin, and that his mum hasn't been told.

rounds.situation: Your friend asks how you could possibly know that. Explain what you spotted online.
rounds.tagalog: Nakita ko kasi 'yung singsing sa IG story niya, tapos dinelete niya agad after five minutes.
rounds.translation: I saw the ring on her IG story, and then she deleted it right away after five minutes.

chunks.note: Kasi ('because') often comes right after the first words in casual talk.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.

chunks.english: then she deleted it right away
chunks.note: Dinelete: an English verb with the Tagalog -in- infix for a completed action.
Manila speakers often switch to English for small numbers and times like this.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Explain that you saw the ring on social media before it was quickly deleted.

lessons.summary: Disagree respectfully with Tito about working abroad or staying home.

content.title: The big debate: working abroad or staying home
content.scenario: Disagree respectfully with Tito about working abroad or staying home.

rounds.situation: At a family lunch, Tito Ramon, a former OFW, insists every young person should work overseas.
rounds.tagalog: Naiintindihan ko po ang punto ninyo, Tito, mas malaki talaga ang sweldo sa abroad.
rounds.translation: I understand your point, Tito; the pay abroad really is much bigger.

chunks.note: Agreeing first is the polite way into a disagreement with an elder.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.

chunks.tagalog: mas malaki talaga ang sweldo sa abroad.
chunks.english: the salary abroad really is bigger
chunks.note: 'Sa abroad' is everyday Taglish for working overseas.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Open by showing him you understand his point about the salary.

rounds.situation: Tito Ramon nods, waiting for your 'but'. Gently bring in the other side.
rounds.tagalog: Pero sa tingin ko po, hindi lahat ng bagay nababayaran ng pera, lalo na 'yung oras kasama ang pamilya.
rounds.translation: But in my view, not everything can be paid for with money, especially time with family.

chunks.note: Sa tingin ko ('the way I see it') is much softer than a flat no.

chunks.tagalog: hindi lahat ng bagay nababayaran ng pera,
chunks.english: not everything can be paid for with money
chunks.note: Nababayaran = can be paid for (abilitative).

chunks.tagalog: lalo na 'yung oras kasama ang pamilya.
chunks.note: Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Respectfully say that money can't buy everything, especially family time.

rounds.situation: Tito Ramon reminds you he spent twelve years in Dubai so his children could study.
rounds.tagalog: Alam ko pong malaki ang naisakripisyo ninyo, kaya nakapagtapos ang mga pinsan ko.
rounds.translation: I know you sacrificed a lot, and that's why my cousins were able to finish school.

chunks.note: Po + the linker -ng becomes 'pong' before the next clause.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.

chunks.tagalog: kaya nakapagtapos ang mga pinsan ko.
chunks.english: that's why my cousins managed to graduate
chunks.note: Nakapag- = managed to; kaya = so, that's why.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Honour his sacrifice and acknowledge what it made possible for your cousins.

content.title: Hay naku, sayang, bahala na: everyday expressions
content.scenario: Miss the last bus with a friend and react like a true local.

rounds.situation: You and your friend Migs run into the Cubao bus terminal, sweaty after an hour stuck on the highway.
rounds.tagalog: Hay naku, ang traffic sa EDSA! Umalis na 'yung huling bus papuntang Baguio.
rounds.translation: Oh man, the traffic on EDSA! The last bus to Baguio already left.

chunks.note: Hay naku is the all-purpose sigh of exasperation.
Ang + noun works as an exclamation: 'such traffic!'.

chunks.tagalog: Umalis na 'yung huling bus papuntang Baguio.
chunks.english: the last bus to Baguio already left
chunks.note: Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Sigh about the traffic and break the news that the last bus is gone.

rounds.situation: Migs waves the two printed tickets you bought online. Now they're useless.
rounds.tagalog: Sayang 'yung ticket natin, binayaran pa naman natin nang buo kahapon!
rounds.translation: What a waste of our tickets, and we even paid for them in full yesterday!

chunks.note: Sayang = 'what a waste, too bad': hard to translate, used constantly.

chunks.english: and to think we even paid for them
chunks.note: Pa naman adds 'and to think we even ...'.
Nang (not ng) introduces how something was done.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Lament the wasted tickets and point out you'd already paid in full.

rounds.situation: There's a provincial bus leaving in ten minutes, with no guarantee of seats. Make the call.
rounds.tagalog: Sige, bahala na! Sakay na lang tayo ng kahit anong bus, basta makarating tayo bago mag-alas dose.
rounds.translation: Okay, come what may! Let's just take any bus, as long as we get there before twelve.

chunks.note: Bahala na = 'leave it to fate': part courage, part shrug.

chunks.tagalog: Sakay na lang tayo ng kahit anong bus,
chunks.note: Na lang = 'just, instead', for a fallback plan.

chunks.tagalog: basta makarating tayo bago mag-alas dose.
chunks.english: as long as we get there before twelve
chunks.note: Clock times use Spanish numbers: alas dose = twelve o'clock.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Decide to risk it: take any bus, as long as you arrive before midnight.

content.title: Forgot the monthsary
content.scenario: You forgot your monthsary. Apologise properly and make it up to them.

rounds.situation: Your partner has been quiet all morning. Then you check the date and realise what you forgot.
rounds.tagalog: Babe, sorry talaga, hindi ko sinasadyang makalimutan 'yung monthsary natin kahapon.
rounds.translation: Babe, I'm really sorry, I didn't mean to forget our monthsary yesterday.

chunks.note: Talaga makes the apology sincere: 'truly'.
Sinasadya = done on purpose; hindi ko sinasadya = I didn't mean it.
Many Filipino couples mark every month together, not just the yearly anniversary.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Apologise sincerely for forgetting your monthsary, and say it wasn't on purpose.

rounds.situation: Your partner crosses their arms and looks away. Don't make excuses; show you understand.
rounds.tagalog: Wala akong maidadahilan, alam kong nasaktan kita, at naiintindihan ko kung bakit ka nagtatampo.
rounds.translation: I have no excuse; I know I hurt you, and I understand why you're upset with me.

chunks.note: Literally 'I have nothing I can give as an excuse'.

chunks.tagalog: at naiintindihan ko kung bakit ka nagtatampo.
chunks.english: and I understand why you're sulking

rounds.speakingPrompt: Admit you have no excuse, that you hurt them, and that their sulking makes sense.

rounds.translation: To make it up to you, I'll cook your favourite sinigang, and then let's catch a movie tonight.

content.scenario: Play Lolo telling how he left the Philippines to work abroad.

rounds.situation: Role-play: you are Lolo. Your grandchild sits beside you on the porch and asks how you ended up abroad.
rounds.tagalog: Apo, noong 1978, umalis ako sa Batangas para magtrabaho bilang construction worker sa Saudi.
rounds.translation: My grandchild, in 1978 I left Batangas to work as a construction worker in Saudi.
